section.para: Stage 2 SMT ingestion and minimal model/result pipeline.

section.title: Scope
section.para: This chapter focuses on sattyre::SMTProblem, parse_smtlib_file, and basic SMTSolver contracts. Early SMT support is text-oriented and intentionally conservative. The target is robust ingestion and explicit errors, not full theory reasoning.

section.title: Input validation
section.para: Missing files, empty content, or malformed command framing should report actionable errors. The loader should preserve original text for later processing. Do not collapse SMT and SAT semantics in this stage.

section.title: SMT result semantics
section.para: SMTSolveResult supports Sat, Unsat, and Unknown. SMTModel currently stores bindings as textual items. The model representation can evolve without invalidating this basic contract.

section.title: CLI interplay
section.para: sattyre-cli should detect .smt2 inputs and route to the SMT parse path. If solver support is not implemented, surface Unknown or an explicit message. Never silently treat SMT as SAT DIMACS input.

literallayout.computeroutput: sattyre-cli examples/example.smt2 # Expect parse success and a clear SMT status path

section.title: Test strategy
section.para: Create good and malformed SMT-LIB examples under tests fixtures. Validate that load failures are deterministic. Keep early tests parser-centric and lightweight.

literallayout.computeroutput: cmake -S . -B build/smt-tests -DSATTYRE_ENABLE_TESTS=ON cmake --build build/smt-tests -j ctest --test-dir build/smt-tests -R sattyre-cli-smoke-test --output-on-failure

section.title: Chapter summary
section.para: SMT stage success means dependable ingestion and clear status reporting. Deep theory support comes later; robust loading is the immediate win. Keep SAT and SMT pathways isolated and explicit.
